page: Amazon Web Services m8id.96xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and dedicated dual-socket Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, the system provides 192 physical cores and 384 vCPUs running at 3.9 GHz, supported by 480 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates 1536 GB of DDR5 memory configured at a 1:4 core-to-memory ratio clocked at 7 GHz. A total of 22800 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage is bundled directly with the host, supplemented by a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. No discrete graphics hardware is present.

Benchmark metrics demonstrate exceptional parallel throughput, placing multi-core compute tests in the top tier. The instance achieved 414823.4 in stress-ng multi-core and 178166.0 in PassMark CPU score, driven by native hardware support for Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets. Memory performance is equally pronounced, recording uncached read bandwidth of 1144.93 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 476.1 GB/sec. Data processing workloads show top-tier results in Redis operations (484.17 million operations per second), static web throughput (198.97 GB/sec), and PassMark database operations. Conversely, single-core metrics fall into average percentiles, and LLM text generation throughput remains constrained without GPU acceleration.

From a resource utilization perspective, the integration of 22.8 TB of fast NVMe storage alongside 1.5 TB of high-speed memory minimizes external storage transfer overhead and latency. This dense configuration provides strong qualitative efficiency for high-density transactional databases, large-scale Redis in-memory caches, distributed compilation, and high-throughput web serving environments requiring immense local scratch space and parallel CPU execution.
